notes: Good fit: mid-market product org, multi-tenant SaaS with 3M monthly search queries; looking to improve relevance without re-architecting pipelines.
Initial ask: reranking endpoint to sit after candidate generation (annoyance scoring + lexical) — want cross-encoder style rerank for top-10 candidates.
Quote from VP Product (A. Mercer): 'If we can move the delta on relevance we convert more trial users; latency tradeoffs are acceptable up to ~200ms p95 for rerank.'

Evaluation plan: 2-week hosted POC using Redwood Hosted API rerank endpoint + offline scoring of historical eval set (50k queries). If NDCG lift and cost look OK, move to Dedicated to guarantee throughput.

Security: customer requires SOC2 attestation, SSO (SAML), KMS integration for keys, and US data residency for indexing/embeddings storage. Legal will need answers to 15-question security questionnaire (attached).
Integration notes: engineering team prefers a simple /rerank endpoint that accepts candidate lists and returns ranked ids + scores and per-document features for explainability.
Ops ask: ability to run large offline batch scoring (100k docs x 50k queries) with CLI or API export of scores for metric calc and A/B evals.
Cost sensitivity: medium-high. Wants quantization recommendations and Optimize suggestions to hit cost target; also interested in prefix/KV caching for common query tails.
Decision process: VP Product owns product decision, CTO leads security review, Procurement on pricing. Buying timeline tied to end of Q2 budget refresh.

use_case_summary: Primary: improve product search relevance via a reranker placed after candidate generation (ANN + lexical).
Secondary: personalization signals (user affinity) fed into reranker, offline model evaluation to measure NDCG and CTR lift.
Key metrics: NDCG@10, CTR on search results, reduction in manual support escalations for search failures.
technical_requirements: Rerank endpoint that accepts batch candidate arrays (ids + features) and returns ranked ids + logits + per-item explainability metadata.
Support for both streaming responses (for live search) and batch/offline scoring API (for overnight re-runs).
Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for rerank top-10 under expected load; target p95 <= 120ms for subset of critical queries.
Throughput target: sustained 40-60 qps for search traffic; occasional spikes up to 150 qps during launches.
Model preferences: open-models welcome (quantized), interested in Redwood's verified latency profiles; cross-encoder recommended for rerank experiments.
Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency + error traces, and exportable logs for offline analysis.
poc_success_criteria: NDCG@10 lift >= 0.06 on Elmfield 50k eval queries vs baseline lexical+ANN pipeline.
Online p95 latency for critical queries stays <= 180ms when routing rerank to Hosted API (with caching + batching).
Cost projection for 1 year (hosted -> dedicated) falls within estimated ARR band or Dedicated pricing makes unit economics 20% better than hosted at scale.
Security signoff: SOC2 presence + SSO integration validated by Elmfield security and SEC-4471 closed.
